tracks.name: Track 0. bb-mrv per-node cost, identical tree
tracks.label: optimization
tracks.note: Judged 20:30 (JUDGE.md 087b301). bb-mrv-fast is node-identical to bb-mrv on all 140 gate instances (judge hashed the original source itself) and 5.3x, 6.1x, 5.3x faster at 6x6, 7x7, 8x8. At 9x9 identity is only checked on capped runs.

tracks.name: Track 1. 9x9 c=11 high-cap pilot, bb-mrv vs scb
tracks.label: measurement
tracks.note: Judged 22:48 (JUDGE.md ba7d7b1). No evidence that bb-mrv's node ratio keeps shrinking at 9x9; the cap of 1e8 decided it (6 of 8 pairs uninformative), not a measured stop. Both informative pairs favour bb-mrv. 27.4 core-hours.

tracks.name: Track 2. A20 blocker eviction as backjump rule
tracks.label: method
tracks.note: Judged 21:08 (JUDGE.md 5dd7adc). Blocker eviction needs 4.7x to 9.2x more nodes than the baselines at 6x6 and solves 5 of 30 at 7x7 against 16 and 23; no better than random eviction. Scope: this repair-search implementation, not backjumping with explanations or stored no-goods.

tracks.name: Track 3. A21 value order by propagation impact
tracks.label: method
tracks.note: Judged 19:16 (JUDGE.md 5c65f77). No node gain against bb-mrv at any rung: 1.075 at 6x6, 0.829 at 7x7, 1.096 at 8x8, all CIs span 1. Judge rerun of 210 rows node-identical.

tracks.name: Track 4. A17 rebaselined: Hall matching on bb-mrv
tracks.label: method
tracks.note: Judged 20:41 (JUDGE.md 67059eb). Hall check on bb-mrv removes under 1% of nodes (0.992 to 1.000) and is slower at every rung where it prunes (wall 1.017 to 1.036). Judge rerun of 1,680 rows node-identical.

tracks.name: Track 5. Baseline tournament
tracks.label: measurement
tracks.note: Judged 23:36 (JUDGE.md 1f4e211). 47 entrants ranked at three rungs; anchors reproduce committed rows (0 mismatches on 1,310), tables recompute exactly. The top two places at R6 and 8x8 are within run-seed noise; at R7 two entrants solve more boards than bb-mrv and the adopted baseline (screening only). 19.1 h against 10 preregistered.

tracks.name: Track 6. Dead-node refutation census (added 20:10)
tracks.label: measurement
tracks.note: Judged 21:26 (JUDGE.md f5f9b9a). Valid measurement, rerun of 13,247 node rows identical, no oracle ever killed a solvable state. Stage-0 kills that stand: cavity summaries (0.8% of dead-node weight), band consistency (0.2%), boundary-word lemmas (0 of 1,447). Cut-keyed partitioning: not decided (the census used a proxy).

tracks.name: Track 7. Partial-match ladder, an instrument (added 20:10)
tracks.label: measurement
tracks.note: Judged 23:35 (JUDGE.md 226baf4). The instrument is not usable as preregistered: 2 of 5 entrants stall in the 2% to 4% band at the one calibrated rung, 3 were needed, and no 10x10 or 12x12 setting qualified. Covers this entrant pool and budget only.

tracks.name: Track 8. Score-bound gap for break-tolerant search (added 20:20)
tracks.label: measurement
tracks.note: Judged 00:48 (JUDGE.md 11a2b91). The bound is sound and passes its kill rule exactly on the threshold (median gap 4 edges at 7x7 with 3 rows left); it loosens as boards grow (1, 2, 4 edges at 2 rows left for 6x6, 7x7, 8x8). Measured on deeply dead prefixes only. 31 thread-hours.

tracks.name: Track 9. Readable and resumable long runs (added 20:45)
tracks.label: optimization
tracks.note: Rejudged 21:55 (JUDGE.md 1ecac8b): every interruption case resumes node for node identical; overhead 1.008 [0.998, 1.011]; the altered-checkpoint defect is fixed (2,202 of 2,202 tampered files refused, plus 658 of 658 on the judge's own). Not measured: resuming a version 2 checkpoint on another machine.

tracks.name: Track 10. Real 16x16 pieces: node profile by depth and tree-width sampling (added 21:46)
tracks.label: measurement
tracks.note: Judged 00:35 (JUDGE.md d601250). Real pieces: the row-scan tree with five clues has 10^40.457 nodes (model 10^40.49), so the price model holds on the real puzzle. In the record-style engine 4.5e-7 of nodes are at or after the first break unlock at 1e10 nodes (budget-dependent; this schedule and port only). Scope narrowed at 01:15: a memo shows this port's colour keying differs from the published record engines, so the late-node share describes this port only.

tracks.name: Track 11. Difference-map search: does the growth rate fall with band width? (added 22:45)
tracks.label: method
tracks.note: Judged 01:51 (JUDGE.md 279118a). The difference-map search solved 0 of 30 near-critical boards at 7x7 and 8x8 at every band width; no band effect at 6x6; wider bands cost more and end further from a solution. No exponent measured. 6.8 core-hours.

tracks.name: Track 12. Cut-keyed partitioning: the deciding replay (added 00:30)
tracks.label: method
tracks.note: Judged 01:04 (JUDGE.md 1828059). A random key with the same number of partitions beats the cut key on 30 of 30 instances at 7x7 (0.419 against 0.486 of bb-mrv's nodes), and the cut costs 1.21 times bb-mrv's propagation work. 2.13 core-hours.

tracks.name: Track 13. Real pieces: colour keying of the record-style engine, legal break path, staging (added 01:15)
tracks.label: measurement
tracks.note: Judged 02:46 (JUDGE.md 17c5688). Real pieces: colour keying changes the node cost of reaching depth 201 by about nothing (1.31 with no clue, 0.74 with the centre clue) and is slower per second; a legal break path gives 4 to 11 times more legal deep nodes per node; the repo's Blackwood-style port differs from the published engine in six ways, one of them a defect. 16.1 thread-hours.

tracks.name: Track 14. Real pieces, five clues: is colour keying a lever? (added 02:38)
tracks.label: measurement
tracks.note: Judged 04:04 (JUDGE.md ee5391c8). Real pieces, five clues: none of 680 published-style keyings reaches legal depth 201 under the scaled quota (0 of 2,040 runs). The comparison with the default keying is confounded with quota slack; Track 15 separates them. 20.6 thread-hours.

tracks.name: Track 15. Real pieces, five clues: is it the quota curve or the port's defect? (added 03:58, last track)
tracks.label: measurement
tracks.note: Judged KEEP (c9088558), 8 reruns identical. Real pieces, five clues: quota slack explains Track 14, not colour. With a loose quota published-style keyings reach depth 201 on 12 to 14 of 16 openings; with a tight quota the default keying is dead. The port's orientation defect is fixed at no cost. 5.67 thread-hours.

tracks.label: no compute
tracks.note: Done, all negative on their own lens: counting and algebra; the designed instance; decompositions; the last ten edges (a 470 board is not a damaged solution: almost all are 246+ cells from any solution); the price (three independent estimates near 1e40 nodes, 17 to 22 orders out of reach).
